idempotency.hash: Server-only HMAC-SHA256 of versioned unambiguous framing: canonical actor/event/operation/idempotency-key scope, method, canonical path, validated default-resolved query, and typed canonical JSON/ABSENT or binary bytes length+digest. Never persist an unkeyed verifier of secret-bearing inputs. The browser neither computes nor receives this fingerprint.
idempotency.tombstone: Retain key/hash until reviewed event/account cleanup; expired result returns IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED, never executes again
idempotency.transaction: Receipt reservation, aggregate guard, mutation, final safe result and outbox are atomic; adapter saga uses downstream same idempotency correlation
idempotency.same_key: Same keyed fingerprint returns only the currently authorized safe receipt/result; changed canonical input conflicts after authorization. Active signing-key rotation alone is not a conflict.
idempotency.retry: No automatic mutation replay; resolve status then explicitly retry identical command/key while retention permits
idempotency.secrets: Never put plaintext pickup code, handle, age proof or token in durable results, outbox or logs. Generic idempotency correlation also uses a server-keyed fingerprint so low-entropy secret input does not become a public/durable unkeyed guessing oracle. A lost one-shot secret response requires explicit rotation/new authorization.

fingerprint.key_source: Trusted injected secret keyring; >=32 random bytes per key. Never from request, database, frontend, source default or log. Keys have immutable identifiers.
fingerprint.rotation: New commands use the active key. Authorized replay verifies against the stored key identifier using retained verification material, never re-signs with the new active key. Retain old verification keys through surviving receipt/tombstone lifetime or explicitly retire those keys without reexecution.
fingerprint.unavailable_key: An unexpired receipt whose verification key is unavailable fails closed DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; an expired or retired key/receipt never executes again. Lost verification capability does not imply changed input or permission to reuse a key.
fingerprint.comparison: Verify the full MAC using the library constant-time verification API only after current authority checks. No unkeyed or legacy format fallback.
fingerprint.privacy: Fingerprint/key IDs are server-internal and absent from CommandReceipt, outbox invalidations and client errors. Public schema rejects request_hash and fingerprint fields. One-shot secret response loss still requires explicit authorized rotation.

status_recovery.lookup: Bind every status response to captured actor, event, requested command and original key; known final target IDs must match. Command response type fixes the expected resource kind. Metadata never substitutes for the authorized resource reread.
status_recovery.unknown_or_inaccessible: 404 RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE deliberately conflates never-recorded, no-longer-visible and unavailable receipt targets. It proves neither nonexecution nor valid retention and NEVER authorizes replay, a new key, or a presumed success.
status_recovery.pending: 202 is PENDING only; status polling is an explicit bounded read. No automatic command replay.
status_recovery.succeeded: SUCCEEDED result_status equals the original command registered success_status, never pending 202 or arbitrary 2xx. Reread current authorized resource/activity before showing current domain state.
status_recovery.failed: FAILED is terminal safe feedback with a reason registered for the original command, not permission to mint a replacement key.
status_recovery.retired_or_expired: RETIRED or expiry never reexecutes. Lost retention or verification cannot justify a new key. Preserve uncertainty and let the user inspect current authorized activity.
status_recovery.retry: The client does not infer retry eligibility from any status alone. Only an explicitly reviewed operation-specific policy with current authorization, original identical input/key and valid retention may allow manual retry; no such automatic policy is enabled here.
